headline: Memphis Mayor Paul Young has signed an order starting a 90-day expert review of how the city should handle data centres.
score_reason: Pool score 5 kept: the order was signed on 9 Oct 2026 and confirmed by several local outlets, but it is a study and does not itself restrict data centres.
importance_line: Memphis residents worried about power, water and air quality get a promised set of rules after a public process, but the order is only a study, it does not pause any project, and the council's own vote is still pending.
summary: The Memphis Flyer reports that Mayor Paul Young signed an executive order on Friday 9 Oct 2026 for a 90-day expert study of data centre rules covering land use, air quality, water, energy costs and noise, with at least three community sessions and a public report, and says it does not delay the City Council. It follows our 8 Oct edition, in which Fox News reported that the council voted 7 to 5 on 6 Oct to put off until 20 Oct its vote on a 12-month pause on new data centres.
notes: Follow-up of 1008:C09-08 (Fox News, our 8 Oct edition item 46). The pool item (The Commercial Appeal) is blocked (HTTP 402), so the report read and credited is the Memphis Flyer's own; the Daily Memphian headline (dailymemphian.com/article/67496/memphis-mayor-paul-young--90-day-data-center-review) confirms the order.
